chapters.summary: Psalm 1 contrasts the way of the righteous with the way of the wicked, declaring that the one who delights in the LORD's law is blessed and will surely be blessed.
keyPoints: Blessed is the one who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, stand in the way of sinners, or sit in the seat of scoffers.
The one who delights in the LORD's law and meditates on it day and night is like a tree planted by streams of water, yielding its fruit in season, its leaves never withering.
The wicked are like chaff that the wind drives away and cannot stand; the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
chapters.application: Meditate daily on God's word and turn away from evil, like a tree rooted by a stream, so that you bear good fruit in every area of life.

chapters.summary: Psalm 2 portrays the futility of the nations rebelling against God and his Anointed, yet God firmly establishes his King and declares blessed all who take refuge in him.
keyPoints: The nations plot in vain, rising up against God and his Anointed, but in the end the LORD only laughs at them.
God sets his King on Zion, granting him authority over the nations to rule them with a rod of iron.
The kings of the earth are warned to be wise and serve God with reverence; blessed are all who take refuge in him.
chapters.application: When we face the world's hostility, let us be confident that God reigns, humbly take refuge in him, and rather than resisting in our own strength, serve him with reverence and joy, enjoying the blessing he gives.

chapters.summary: Psalm 3 was written by David during Absalom's rebellion, expressing his confidence in relying on God and finding peace even as enemies surround him.
keyPoints: David faces many enemies, but God is his shield and his glory.
Even in his distress David can lie down and sleep in peace, because God watches over and sustains him.
David asks God to save him and declares that salvation belongs to the LORD.
chapters.application: When you feel surrounded on every side, do as David did: turn your eyes from your circumstances to God, and trust that he is your shield who grants you a peace beyond understanding.

chapters.summary: Psalm 4 is David crying out to God in distress, urging others to trust in God and offer righteous sacrifices, because God gives a joy and peace that surpasses all else.
keyPoints: David asks God to answer him, for God has comforted him in distress before; he pleads for mercy and for his prayer to be heard.
He urges others to fear God and not sin, to search their own hearts in silence, and to offer righteous sacrifices while trusting in the LORD.
He declares that God puts more joy in his heart than an abundance of grain and new wine, and that he can lie down and sleep in peace because God keeps him safe.
chapters.application: When you feel wronged or anxious, come quietly before God, lay down your burdens, and trust in his righteousness and care - then you will know the peace he gives, and rest in sleep.

chapters.summary: David cries out to God in the morning, asking him to hear his prayer, and declares that God hates wickedness while the righteous will surely be blessed.
keyPoints: David cries out to God in the morning, expressing his trust in and dependence on him.
God is righteous; he hates those who do evil and will judge the wicked.
Those who take refuge in God will find joy and protection, as though surrounded by a shield.
chapters.application: Bring your prayers to God every morning, trusting that he will hear you. Turn away from evil, take refuge in his steadfast love, and he will give you joy and peace.

chapters.summary: In sickness and under attack from his enemies, David cries out for God's mercy; confident that God will hear him, his lament turns at last into praise.
keyPoints: David asks God not to rebuke him in anger, confessing his own weakness and frailty.
He describes his anguish of body and soul, weeping without ceasing, and pleads for God to turn and save him.
He is confident that God has heard his prayer, and that his enemies will be put to shame and driven back.
chapters.application: When we are in distress, we can pour out our hearts to God as David did, trusting that he will hear us, and wait for his deliverance.

chapters.summary: When falsely accused and pursued, David cries out to God for righteous judgment, confident that God will repay the wicked according to justice, and gives thanks for God's righteousness.
keyPoints: David asks God to save him from all who pursue him, and pleads his own innocence.
David calls on God to judge with righteousness, that the wicked be punished and the righteous be established.
David declares that God is a righteous judge, angry with the wicked every day, and that he will protect the upright.
chapters.application: When wronged, pour out your heart to God as David did, trust that he will judge with righteousness, hold fast to integrity while you wait, and end in praise.

chapters.summary: The psalmist praises God's majesty across the universe, and marvels that God cares for humanity, crowning us with glory and honor and giving us dominion over his creation.
keyPoints: How excellent is the name of the LORD in all the earth; his glory is displayed above the heavens.
Out of the mouths of babes and infants God has established strength, silencing the enemy.
Though man is so small, God is mindful of him, crowning him with glory and honor and giving him dominion over the works of his hands.
chapters.application: When the vastness of the universe makes us feel small, remember that God is mindful of us and gives us dignity and purpose. Let us gratefully steward the dominion he has given, caring for creation and giving glory to his name.

chapters.summary: David praises God amid affliction, because God judges the wicked and vindicates the oppressed, and he calls people to look to God's righteousness.
keyPoints: David gives thanks to God with his whole heart, telling of his wonderful works.
God judges the wicked and blots out their name forever.
God is a stronghold for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
chapters.application: In hard times, remember that God is a righteous judge who watches over you. As David did, begin your prayer with praise and lay your burdens on God - he will be your stronghold and refuge.

chapters.summary: The psalmist laments the prosperity of the wicked and cries out for God to establish justice, confident that God cares for the afflicted.
keyPoints: The wicked boast in pride and oppress the afflicted, saying in their hearts that God will not call them to account.
The psalmist cries out for God to arise and lift up his hand, not to forget the afflicted, and to break the arm of the wicked.
He is confident that God hears the desire of the humble and will vindicate the fatherless and the oppressed.
chapters.application: When you see the wicked prosper, do not lose heart. Pour out your heart to God as the psalmist did, trusting that he sees all things and will bring about justice in his own time.

chapters.summary: Facing attack from the wicked, the psalmist firmly trusts in the LORD, declaring that God will judge the wicked and protect the upright.
keyPoints: The psalmist refuses to flee, choosing instead to take refuge in the LORD.
God observes mankind from his holy temple and tests the righteous.
God will rain fire and brimstone on the wicked, while the righteous will behold his face.
chapters.application: When circumstances look dangerous, we can still trust God with our whole heart, for he governs all things and will watch over the righteous and judge the wicked.

chapters.summary: The psalmist asks God to save him from those who speak falsehood, confident that God's pure words will keep those who belong to him.
keyPoints: People speak lies with a double heart, and the wicked prowl everywhere.
The psalmist asks God to cut off flattering lips and boastful tongues.
God's words are pure, and he will preserve the godly from this generation.
chapters.application: When surrounded by lies, turn to God - his word is trustworthy, and he will watch over those who belong to him, a stronghold in times of trouble.

chapters.summary: Psalm 13 is David's lament crying out to God in distress; he expresses his confusion at God's delay, but ends by trusting in God's steadfast love and salvation.
keyPoints: David asks how long God will forget him, giving voice to the pain and helplessness deep within him.
He asks God to look upon him and answer, lest his enemies boast over him - revealing his longing for God's deliverance.
In the end he turns to trust in God's steadfast love, rejoicing in God's salvation, and responds with praise.
chapters.application: When God seems distant, pour out your heart honestly as David did, and choose to trust in his steadfast love, rejoicing in the salvation he gives.

chapters.summary: Psalm 14 describes the fool who denies God, yet God watches over the righteous and promises that salvation will come out of Zion.
keyPoints: The fool says in his heart there is no God; his deeds are corrupt, and there is none who does good.
God looks down from heaven on the children of man, but there is none who does good, and all have turned aside.
Evildoers oppress the righteous, yet God is with the righteous, and he will restore the fortunes of his captive people.
chapters.application: When the world denies God, let us hold fast to our faith, for God watches over the righteous and has promised deliverance - let us rely on him in times of trouble.

chapters.summary: Psalm 15 describes the character and conduct required of one who would dwell in God's tent and live on his holy hill, emphasizing honesty, righteousness, and faithfulness.
keyPoints: The one who walks blamelessly, does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart may draw near to God.
The one who does not slander, does not wrong a friend, and does not join in reproaching a neighbor shows love for his neighbor as himself.
The one who honors and fears the LORD, who keeps an oath even to his own hurt and does not lend on usury, will never be moved.
chapters.application: Examine whether your words and deeds are honest and righteous. Treat others with a heart that fears God, keep your promises, and refuse unjust gain - and you will be firmly established.

chapters.summary: The psalmist expresses his trust in God, treasuring him above all else, rejoicing in his presence, and confident that God will never abandon him but will show him the path of life.
keyPoints: The psalmist declares that the LORD is his Master, and apart from him he has no good thing.
He counts God as his inheritance and the portion of his cup, and his heart and soul rejoice.
He is confident that God will make known to him the path of life, will not abandon his holy one, and will give him fullness of joy.
chapters.application: Today, let God be the source of your contentment. Trust him in every circumstance, for he will show you the path, and give you true joy and hope.

chapters.summary: In distress David asks God for vindication, declaring his own integrity, pleading for God's protection from the wicked, and longing to behold God's face.
keyPoints: David asks God to hear his prayer, for he has lived uprightly and his lips have not spoken deceit.
David asks God to show his wonderful steadfast love, protecting him as the apple of his eye.
David is confident that he will behold God's face, and that beholding him in righteousness will fully satisfy him.
chapters.application: When we are wrongly accused or treated unjustly, we can pour out our hearts to God as David did, trusting that he watches over us, and finding our satisfaction in his presence.

chapters.summary: After being delivered from Saul and all his enemies, David praises the LORD as his rock and his deliverer, describing God's mighty salvation and his righteousness.
keyPoints: With deep love David declares that the LORD is his strength, his rock, his fortress, and his savior.
In his distress he cried out, and God heard him and shook heaven and earth, delivering him with great power.
God repays each person according to righteousness and purity, displaying his faithfulness and steadfast love.
chapters.application: Whatever hardship we face, let us cry out to God as David did, trusting that he will hear and deliver us. May we constantly praise him with a grateful heart for his works.

chapters.summary: Psalm 19 praises God for revealing himself through nature and through the law, expressing love for God's word and a prayer for a clean heart.
keyPoints: The heavens and the sky declare God's glory and his handiwork without a single word spoken.
God's law is perfect, sure, and right, reviving the soul and making the simple wise.
The psalmist asks God to forgive his hidden faults and keep him from willful sin.
chapters.application: Take notice each day of the beauty of creation, meditate on God's word, and ask him to reveal and cleanse the sins within us, that we may live a life pleasing to him.

chapters.summary: Psalm 20 is a prayer offered before a king goes to battle, asking God to answer the people's petitions and expressing confidence that God will save his anointed, triumphing in the name of the LORD.
keyPoints: The people offer sacrifices and pray for the king, asking God to answer him and protect him in trouble.
Some trust in chariots and horses, but true victory comes from the name of the LORD.
They are confident that God will fulfill their petitions, for he is God's anointed, and salvation belongs to the LORD.
chapters.application: In hardship we often rely on visible resources, but only the name of the LORD is a sure defense. Let us entrust everything to him and look to him in faith, and we will see his salvation.

chapters.summary: David, as king, rejoices in the LORD's strength and salvation, giving thanks for the victory and blessing God has given him.
keyPoints: The king rejoices in God's salvation and praises his strength.
God grants the king his heart's desire, crowning him with a crown of pure gold.
The king triumphs by God's hand, and his enemies are destroyed by God.
chapters.application: When we experience success in life, let us remember that it is God's grace; let us give him thanks and continue to rely on him.

chapters.summary: Psalm 22 describes David's cry from the depths of his suffering, while also foreshadowing the Anointed One's suffering and his ultimate triumph.
keyPoints: David laments that God has forsaken him, enduring the scorn and attacks of his enemies.
He recalls how his ancestors trusted God and were delivered, while he himself is despised like a worm.
He prophesies that the nations will turn to God, declaring that his righteousness and salvation will be proclaimed to generations to come.
chapters.application: When we feel forsaken, let us pour out our hearts to God as David did, remembering his faithfulness. He has triumphed over suffering, and we can wait in faith for his deliverance.

chapters.summary: The LORD is our shepherd, providing, guiding, and protecting, so that those who trust him find rest and grace.
keyPoints: God is our shepherd, providing everything we need, so that we shall not want.
In times of trouble, God is present with us, giving comfort and guidance.
Goodness and mercy follow us all our days, and we shall dwell in the house of the LORD.
chapters.application: When you feel lacking or afraid, remind yourself that God is your shepherd - he will guide you, protect you, and give you sufficient grace, so that you can rest in trust.

chapters.summary: Psalm 24 declares that God is the sovereign Lord of the earth, and calls people to purify themselves to welcome the King of glory.
keyPoints: The earth and everything in it belongs to the LORD, for he founded it upon the seas.
The one with clean hands and a pure heart, who does not worship idols or swear falsely, may ascend the hill of the LORD.
The King of glory is the LORD of hosts, and he will enter the gates in triumph.
chapters.application: Let us examine our thoughts and deeds, welcoming the Lord with a pure heart. In daily life let us enthrone God as King, confident that he will bless those who seek him.

chapters.summary: In distress David asks God for guidance, forgiveness, and protection, expressing his steadfast trust in and dependence on God.
keyPoints: He asks God not to let those who trust in him be put to shame, showing his resolve to depend on God.
He pleads with God to remember his mercy and steadfast love, and to forgive the sins of his youth.
He acknowledges that God guides sinners in the right way, and teaches the humble his ways.
chapters.application: When you feel lost or ashamed, follow David's example - lift up your heart to God, ask him to guide your path, and trust that he will deal with you in steadfast love.

chapters.summary: David professes his integrity before God, asking God to examine and test him, declaring that he has kept away from evildoers, and longing to worship God in the sanctuary.
keyPoints: David asks God to vindicate him, for he has walked in integrity and trusted in the LORD without wavering.
David declares that he hates the assembly of evildoers and will not sit with the deceitful and the wicked.
David longs to give thanks at God's altar and to tell of all his wonderful works.
chapters.application: In a complicated world, let us follow David's example - hold fast to a pure heart, keep away from evil, and draw near to God continually, that we may be guided in worship.

chapters.summary: Psalm 27 shows David, in the midst of distress, expressing his trust in and longing for God, confident that God will watch over and guide him all his life.
keyPoints: The LORD is his light and his salvation, so he fears nothing.
He longs to dwell in the house of the LORD all his life, gazing upon his beauty.
Even in trouble he will still wait for the LORD, taking courage and being strong.
chapters.application: When facing difficulty, remember that God is your light and salvation. Seek him wholeheartedly, wait patiently, and he will strengthen your heart.

chapters.summary: In distress David cries out to the LORD, pleading with God to hear him and to judge the wicked; trusting in God he finds strength and help, and ends with praise and thanksgiving.
keyPoints: David earnestly cries out to God, for if God does not hear him he will be like those who go down to the pit.
He asks God to repay the wicked according to their deeds, because they disregard the works of the LORD.
The LORD is David's strength and shield; he trusts in him, and his heart rejoices and gives thanks.
chapters.application: In hardship, pour out your heart to God as David did, trusting that he will hear you; and take notice of his works, responding to his faithfulness with a grateful heart.

chapters.summary: Psalm 29 describes the LORD's voice as full of power, displaying his glory and giving his people peace.
keyPoints: It calls on the heavenly beings to ascribe glory to the LORD and worship him in the splendor of holiness.
The LORD's voice is like thunder, breaking the cedars and shaking the wilderness, displaying his great power.
The LORD sits enthroned as King, giving strength and peace to his people.
chapters.application: When life is as turbulent as a storm, remember that God's voice carries power; he sits enthroned as King and will give you strength and peace.

chapters.summary: After recovering from illness, David offers thanks, praising God for lifting his soul up from the grave and delivering him from suffering.
keyPoints: David praises God for healing him, acknowledging that God's anger lasts only a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime.
David once boasted in his prosperity, but was dismayed when God hid his face - showing that our security rests in God's favor alone.
David asks God to hear his cry; God turned his mourning into dancing, clothed him with gladness, and he will give thanks to God forever.
chapters.application: In good times, do not forget God's grace; in hard times, cry out to him. God's anger is momentary, but his favor endures - he can turn your mourning into dancing and clothe you with gladness and praise.

chapters.summary: Psalm 31 is David's prayer in distress, expressing his trust in and surrender to God, and ending with praise and encouragement.
keyPoints: David asks God to deliver him in his righteousness and rescue him from the enemy's net.
He declares that God is his refuge, and commits his spirit into God's hand.
Though his strength fails through affliction, he remains confident that God will show him grace.
chapters.application: In hardship, surrender everything to God as David did, trust that he watches over you, and wait for his deliverance in faith.

chapters.summary: Having experienced the grace of forgiveness, David testifies to God's faithful care, and urges others to confess their sin to God and rely on his steadfast love.
keyPoints: Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven and whose sin is covered.
When he kept silent about his sin, his body and spirit wasted away, but once he confessed to God he was forgiven.
Steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts in God, but the wicked will have many sorrows.
chapters.application: Confess your sins openly to God; there is no need to hide them. He will forgive and guide us, and we will find peace and joy in prayer.

chapters.summary: This psalm calls the righteous to praise God, for he created heaven and earth by his word, and he watches over those who fear him, granting steadfast love and salvation.
keyPoints: The righteous should praise God with shouts of joy and with the lyre and harp, for praise befits the upright.
By his word God made the heavens, and by the breath of his mouth all their host, displaying his great power.
Those who fear God will be watched over; his eye is on them, to deliver them from death.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, remember that God is the Creator who watches over those who fear him. Begin today with praise, trust in his steadfast love, and you will find security.

chapters.summary: In distress David praises God, urging everyone to fear the LORD, for he watches over the righteous and delivers them.
keyPoints: David feigned madness before Abimelech, and after escaping he gave thanks to God.
He urges everyone to taste and see that the LORD is good - those who fear him lack nothing.
God is near to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit; the righteous will be kept safe.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, praise God continually; cry out to him in trouble, and he will hear you and deliver you from fear.

chapters.summary: Under attack from enemies, David cries out to God for vindication, and praises God's righteousness and salvation.
keyPoints: David asks God to be his shield and to fight on his behalf, contending against his enemies.
His enemies hate him without cause and repay evil for good, yet David has treated them with kindness.
David is confident that God will bring about justice, and so he will give thanks and praise God in the great assembly.
chapters.application: When you suffer injustice, entrust your grievance to God, trust that he watches over you, keep overcoming evil with good, and in the end give him thanks.

chapters.summary: Psalm 36 contrasts the sin of the wicked with the steadfast love of God, praising his faithfulness, righteousness, and watchful care, and asking God to preserve the righteous.
keyPoints: The wicked have no fear of God in their hearts, deceiving themselves, speaking falsely, and plotting evil.
God's steadfast love reaches to the heavens, his faithfulness to the clouds, his righteousness is like the mighty mountains, and his judgments like the great deep.
God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light - the psalmist asks God to continue his steadfast love to those who know him.
chapters.application: When facing injustice in the world, look to God's steadfast love and faithfulness - he watches over the righteous, and those who take refuge in him will be satisfied and given the light of life.

chapters.summary: This psalm urges trust in God, warning against fretting over the prosperity of the wicked, and promising that those who wait on God will inherit the land.
keyPoints: Do not fret over evildoers; instead trust in the LORD and do good.
Commit your way to the LORD, and he will bring about your righteousness.
The wicked will in the end be cut off, but the humble will inherit the land.
chapters.application: When facing injustice, meditate on God's promises, overcome evil with good, cast your burdens on the Lord, and rest in him.

chapters.summary: In sickness and guilt, David cries out to the LORD for mercy, confesses his sin, and looks to God for deliverance.
keyPoints: David suffers in body and soul under God's discipline because of his sin.
He confesses his iniquity, grieving over it in sorrow before God.
Surrounded by enemies, he still looks to God and asks him to hurry to help him.
chapters.application: When we suffer for our sin, let us follow David's example - confess honestly to God, do not flee his discipline, and trust firmly that he will not forsake us but will graciously deliver us.

chapters.summary: In affliction the psalmist asks God to help him understand the brevity of life, and looks for God's forgiveness and deliverance.
keyPoints: The psalmist resolves to guard his words carefully, lest he sin against God.
He laments that life is as brief as a breath, and that all his labor is vanity.
He asks God to turn away his punishment, for he is merely a sojourner passing through.
chapters.application: Let us number our days and gain a heart of wisdom, placing our hope in God through our limited years, and not despairing in affliction.

chapters.summary: In distress David waits patiently for God, sings praise for his salvation, and declares his delight in doing God's will.
keyPoints: David waited patiently for the LORD, who heard his cry and lifted him out of the pit and the miry clay.
God put a new song in David's mouth, so that many would see and fear, and put their trust in the LORD.
David declares that he delights to do God's will, and proclaims his righteousness and faithfulness.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us wait patiently for God as David did, trusting that he will hear our cry. And let us obey God with a grateful heart, testifying in our lives to his wonderful works.

chapters.summary: This psalm is David's prayer amid sickness and enemy attack, confident that God watches over and cares for the poor, and will preserve his life.
keyPoints: Blessed is the one who considers the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble.
The curses of his enemies and the betrayal of false friends bring him deep pain.
David cries out for mercy, confident that God will sustain and uphold him.
chapters.application: When we treat others kindly, God takes note; in sickness or hardship, let us pour out our hearts to God as David did, trusting that he watches over us.

chapters.summary: Psalm 42 expresses a deep longing for God, holding fast to hope even amid adversity, confident that God will show his grace.
keyPoints: As a deer pants for streams of water, so the psalmist expresses his intense longing for God.
In exile he recalls the worship of former days, and his soul is downcast.
He encourages himself to hope in God, for God's smile will bring help.
chapters.application: When your soul is downcast, pour out your heart to God as the psalmist did, and remind yourself: God is my help, and I will hope in him - he will restore my joy.

chapters.summary: The psalmist asks God to vindicate him, recalling the joy of walking with God in former days amid his affliction, and encourages himself to hope in God, who is his help and the light of his countenance.
keyPoints: The psalmist asks God to vindicate him and deliver him from a deceitful and unjust people.
He recalls the joy of former days in God's sanctuary, and longs to return to God's presence.
His soul is downcast and troubled within him, but he chooses to hope in God, calling him his help and his glory.
chapters.application: When you feel misunderstood or alone, pour out your heart to God as the psalmist did, and remind yourself: God is the light of your countenance, he will guide you, and renew your strength.

chapters.summary: Psalm 44 is a lament of the people crying out to God for help amid defeat and disgrace; they recall God's past deliverances and express their steadfast trust in him.
keyPoints: They recall God's wondrous works in the days of their ancestors, showing that God is the source of salvation.
They acknowledge that the people trusted in God, not in their own strength, yet now they are cast off and put to shame by God.
Even in suffering they hold fast to their faith, crying out for God to arise and show grace, refusing to forsake him despite persecution.
chapters.application: When life brings setbacks, or God seems to have forgotten us, let us still hold fast to faith, pour out our hearts to God, and trust that his steadfast love never changes and that he watches over us.

chapters.summary: This is a song of praise for a royal wedding, foreshadowing the union of the Anointed One and his people, displaying the King's glory and righteousness.
keyPoints: It praises the King's beauty and majesty, his victory and righteousness blessed by God.
It describes the King's bride, urging her to forget her people and her father's house, and to give herself wholly to the King.
It prophesies that the King's descendants will inherit the throne, and his name will be remembered through all generations.
themes: The Promise of an Eternal Kingdom
chapters.application: Let us follow the Anointed One with reverence and obedience, for he is worthy of all honor; and let us remain faithful to him with a pure heart, waiting for his glorious return.

chapters.summary: Psalm 46 declares that God is the refuge and strength of believers in trouble; even if the earth and heavens shake, God is present and gives peace.
keyPoints: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Even if the earth trembles and the mountains shake, and the sea roars, we will not fear, for God is with us.
God will help within the city and make it secure; his power brings wars to an end.
chapters.application: When facing turmoil and unrest, quiet your heart and rely on God - he is our refuge, and he will give us peace and strength.

chapters.summary: Psalm 47 praises God as the great King over all the earth, calling all peoples to shout for joy, for he rules over the nations, and the Holy One of Israel is exalted.
keyPoints: All peoples are called to clap their hands and shout for joy, for the LORD is the great and awesome King.
God chose an inheritance for Israel, and ascends with a shout - he is worthy of praise.
God reigns as King over the nations, and the kings of the earth submit to him.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, praise God with a joyful heart, for he reigns. In daily life, remind yourself: God is King, and he will lead us to victory.

chapters.summary: Psalm 48 praises Mount Zion as God's holy city, in which God shows himself a sure refuge; kings who see it are struck with terror, and God will establish this city forever.
keyPoints: God is great in the city of Zion, and is worthy of praise in all the earth.
Kings gathered together to attack, but when they saw what God had done they were struck with terror and fled.
God will establish Zion forever, and will be our guide.
themes: The Security of the Holy City
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, God is our sure stronghold. In times of anxiety, meditate on his faithfulness, and let him be your guide forever.

chapters.summary: Psalm 49 teaches all people that wealth cannot redeem a life; only God can redeem us from death.
keyPoints: It calls all peoples, rich and poor alike, to give heed to words of wisdom.
Riches cannot ransom a life; no one can bribe God to escape death.
The wise die just as the foolish do, but God will redeem the righteous.
chapters.application: Do not put your trust in riches, but in God. In the face of death's threat, only God can redeem us and grant us eternal life.

chapters.summary: God summons heaven and earth as witnesses and judges his people, showing that sacrifices cannot substitute for genuine worship and thanksgiving.
keyPoints: God shines forth from Zion, summoning his people and heaven and earth as witnesses to carry out judgment.
God has no need of offerings, for everything belongs to him; the true sacrifice is thanksgiving and trust.
He rebukes the wicked for feigning worship, warns those who forget God, and promises salvation to those who walk uprightly.
chapters.application: Reflect on your spiritual life - do you focus on outward form while neglecting your heart? Draw near to God with a grateful heart, call on him in trouble, and he will deliver you.

chapters.summary: After his sin, David pleads with God for mercy, begs him to wash away his guilt, and asks him to restore within him a clean heart and a right spirit.
keyPoints: David confesses his sin and pleads with God, according to his lovingkindness, to blot out his transgressions.
He asks God to purge him with hyssop and wash away his iniquity, that he may again hear the sound of joy and gladness.
He asks God to create in him a clean heart and renew a right spirit within him.
chapters.application: When we fall, let us not hide our sin, but come openly before God to confess it, trusting that his mercy will wash us clean and give us a new beginning.

chapters.summary: Psalm 52 condemns the wicked for trusting in wealth and lies, while declaring that the righteous will stand firm through God's steadfast love, and praises God's justice.
keyPoints: The wicked man harms others with his tongue and boasts in his evil, not knowing that God will destroy him.
The righteous see the wicked man's downfall, fear God, and rejoice in God's justice.
The psalmist likens himself to a green olive tree, trusting in God's steadfast love and never to be shaken.
chapters.application: When facing injustice or harsh words, do not let your heart resent it; trust in God's justice, overcome evil with good, and stay rooted like an olive tree ever growing in God's house.

chapters.summary: The fool says in his heart there is no God; he does evil, but God will judge, and the righteous will rejoice.
keyPoints: The fool denies God and lives corruptly; there is none who does good.
God looks down from heaven upon mankind, but finds no one who seeks him.
The wicked will be rejected by God, but the righteous will find salvation and joy.
chapters.application: When people deny God, life loses its direction. Let us trust in God, turn away from folly, look to his salvation in hardship, and rejoice in his justice.

chapters.summary: In distress David cries out to God, confident that God will save him, and vows to offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to him.
keyPoints: David asks God to save him by his name and vindicate him by his might.
He declares that God will repay the wicked and destroy the treacherous.
He vows to offer a freewill sacrifice and praise God's name, for God has delivered him from trouble.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us cry out to God as David did, confident that he watches over us, and let us keep a thankful heart, answering God's deliverance with action.

chapters.summary: Psalm 55 is David's lament amid betrayal and attack; he cries out to God for deliverance, voices his anger at his enemies and the traitor among them, and finally casts his burden on God, confident that God will sustain the righteous.
keyPoints: David pours out the anguish of his heart and asks God to listen to his prayer.
He denounces the wickedness of the betrayer and longs to escape his distress.
He urges people to cast their burden on God, trusting that God will sustain them.
chapters.application: When you suffer a friend's betrayal or find yourself in distress, follow David's example: hand your worries over to God, confident that he will sustain you and keep you standing firm.

chapters.summary: Pursued by his enemies, David cries out to God, confident that God takes note of his tears, and relies on God's promises to praise him.
keyPoints: David asks for mercy, for his enemies oppress and attack him all day long.
God knows David's wanderings, counts his tears, and records them in his book.
David declares his trust in God and praise for his word, no longer fearing what man can do to him.
chapters.application: When you feel surrounded, remember that God counts your tears and watches over you. Hand your fears to God and praise him in faith, for he is your helper.

chapters.summary: In danger David cries out to God, confident that God will show him steadfast love and faithfulness, and longs for God to be exalted over all the earth.
keyPoints: Pursued by his enemies, David takes refuge in God and asks for mercy.
He praises God's steadfast love and faithfulness, holding firm in faith even in peril.
He declares that God will bring deliverance, and prays that God be exalted, his glory filling the whole earth.
chapters.application: In times of distress, let us cry out to God as David did, trusting in his steadfast love and faithfulness, and long for his name to be glorified.

chapters.summary: David calls on God to judge unjust judges, and expresses his confidence that the wicked will finally be repaid.
keyPoints: He rebukes human judges for their injustice and violence, for their hearts devise evil.
He describes the wicked as deaf as a serpent that will not heed the charmer's voice, and declares they will be struck down by God.
The righteous rejoice at seeing the wicked repaid, confident that God executes righteous judgment.
chapters.application: When you face injustice, hand your grievance over to God, confident that he will judge righteously, and wait in faith for him to act.

chapters.summary: Hunted by Saul, David asks God to save him from his enemies, and confident that God will judge the wicked, closes with praise.
keyPoints: He asks God to deliver him from fierce enemies, for they lie in wait to attack the innocent.
The wicked surround him like dogs, but God will laugh at the nations and execute judgment.
The psalmist sings praise to God, for God is his high tower and refuge.
chapters.application: When you face injustice or attack, cry out to God as David did, confident that he watches over you, and answer fear with praise.

chapters.summary: In national crisis David cries out to God, confident that God will bring deliverance, and relies on God to prevail over his enemies.
keyPoints: David acknowledges that God has once allowed his people to suffer defeat, and asks God to restore them.
God promises victory, and David declares in faith that they will prevail.
Only by relying on God can they display his mighty power and trample down their enemies.
chapters.application: When setbacks come, pour out your heart to God as David did, trust in his promises, and rely on his mighty power to find strength and hope in hardship.

chapters.summary: Psalm 61 is David's cry to God in distress, expressing confidence in God's protection and praying for the king to reign under God's care for long years.
keyPoints: Far from safety, David cries to God from the end of the earth, showing that even in his direst extremity he still looks to God.
He asks God to lead him to a rock higher than himself, a picture of asking God for firm shelter and strength.
David is confident that God will answer his prayer, and vows to fulfill his vows before God, showing his devotion to God.
chapters.application: When you feel alone or helpless, cry out to God as David did; he is your rock and refuge, and he will hear your prayer and give you peace.

chapters.summary: Psalm 62 teaches us to wait on God alone, rooting our trust in his salvation and his rock rather than in man or riches.
keyPoints: My soul waits in silence for God alone, for my salvation comes from him.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, my high tower; I shall not be greatly shaken.
Do not trust in man or in riches; power belongs to God, and steadfast love also belongs to him.
chapters.application: When the pressures of life come upon you, be still before God first, meditate on his promises, and cast your burden on him, for he is a rock you can rely on.

chapters.summary: Psalm 63 is the psalmist's longing for and praise of God in the wilderness, expressing his confidence that God alone satisfies even amid hardship.
keyPoints: The psalmist earnestly seeks God, as a dry and thirsty land longs for water, expressing his deep longing for God.
He beholds God's power and glory in the sanctuary, for God's steadfast love is better than life.
He remembers God in the night and praises him with joyful lips; he clings close to God, whose right hand upholds him, and his enemies will be subdued.
chapters.application: In the wilderness of life, pour out your heart to God, delight in him, and be confident of his support and deliverance, so that your soul finds true satisfaction.

chapters.summary: David asks God for protection, exposes the schemes of his enemies, and is confident that God will judge them righteously, bringing joy to the righteous.
keyPoints: David asks God to hear his voice and protect his life from the terror of the enemy.
He describes the wicked plotting secretly, wounding with their words, thinking no one sees.
God will shoot them with an arrow, wounding them suddenly, so that all who see will be afraid.
chapters.application: When someone harms you in secret, do not be afraid, for God sees everything and will vindicate you. Simply trust in him, and he will protect you.

chapters.summary: Psalm 65 praises God for forgiving sin, creating and caring for the earth by his might, and making all things abundant, displaying his steadfast love and care.
keyPoints: God hears prayer and forgives our transgressions, letting us draw near to him.
God settles the mountains by his strength and stills the roaring of the waves, revealing his power.
God cares for the earth and sends down rain, making the grain abundant and filling the land with gladness.
chapters.application: When you are in hardship, remember that God is the Lord who forgives sin and cares for his creation. He sends rain and harvest, and he will supply all your needs as well. Bring him your worries with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: Psalm 66 calls the whole earth to praise God for his mighty deeds throughout history, and teaches that individuals experience God's faithfulness and deliverance in their own troubles.
keyPoints: It calls the whole earth to shout for joy and sing praise to God, for his works are great and awesome.
It recalls God's wondrous deliverance at the exodus and the crossing of the Red Sea.
In his own affliction the psalmist made vows to God and testifies that God heard his prayer.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, remember the wonders God has done, pour out your heart to him, and testify to his faithfulness, drawing strength from praise.

chapters.summary: Psalm 67 is a thanksgiving psalm asking God to bless Israel, that all peoples may know his salvation, and calling the nations to praise him.
keyPoints: It asks God to be merciful and bless us, and let his face shine upon us, that the whole earth may know his ways.
It calls all peoples to praise God, for he judges the peoples with equity and guides the nations of the earth.
The earth has yielded its increase, God has blessed Israel, and all the ends of the earth will fear him.
chapters.application: Let us always give thanks for God's blessings, and ask him to make us channels of blessing, so that more people come to know his salvation and join in praising him.

chapters.summary: Psalm 68 praises God's might, describing how he led Israel out of Egypt and into the sanctuary, and calls all nations to praise him.
keyPoints: God arises and scatters his enemies; the righteous rejoice, and the wicked perish like smoke.
God cares for the fatherless and the widow, gives the lonely a home, and sets prisoners free into prosperity.
God protects his people with his mighty power and gives them authority; let the nations sing praises to him.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, remember that God is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows. He gives strength and power day by day; let us praise his deeds continually.

chapters.summary: Psalm 69 is a personal lament; David cries to God from deep waters, pleading for deliverance from persecution by his enemies, and foretells judgment on the wicked.
keyPoints: David uses the image of overwhelming floodwaters to express his profound anguish and helplessness.
He acknowledges his own folly and sin, but stresses that he bears reproach for God's sake.
He asks God to save him by his steadfast love and faithfulness, and calls down judgment on his enemies, wishing them blotted out of the book of life.
chapters.application: When you feel overwhelmed in hardship, pour out your heart to God as David did, trust that he hears you, and find hope and strength in his promises.

chapters.summary: In urgent distress David cries to God for swift help, asks that his enemies be put to shame, and declares that God is great, resolving to rejoice and praise God despite his own poverty and need.
keyPoints: David pleads with God to hasten to deliver him without delay.
He asks that those who seek his life be turned back in disgrace.
He declares that God is great, and that those who fear God will rejoice in him.
chapters.application: When hardship comes, we may boldly ask God, as David did, to help us quickly, and trust that he watches over us, offering praise as a sacrifice even as we wait, for God alone is our refuge.

chapters.summary: In old age the psalmist asks God for deliverance, relies on God's righteousness and salvation, and praises God's faithfulness.
keyPoints: The psalmist asks God to be his refuge and save him from the hand of the wicked.
He has trusted in God since youth, and in old age still asks God not to forsake him.
He declares God's righteousness and salvation, and resolves to proclaim God's might.
chapters.application: Whatever our age, God is always our rock. In hardship, let us cry out to him as the psalmist did, and proclaim his faithfulness all our lives.

chapters.summary: This psalm asks God to give the king righteousness and justice, that he may judge the people justly, bringing a peaceful, prosperous reign and blessing to the whole world.
keyPoints: It asks God to give the king righteousness, that he may judge the people and the afflicted with justice.
The king comes like rain, bringing righteousness and abundance, and the needy find deliverance.
His dominion stretches from sea to sea; all nations will be blessed through him and call him blessed.
chapters.application: Let us pursue righteousness in our lives, treat the needy with kindness, and hope for the full coming of Christ's kingdom, that the whole earth may enjoy peace and blessing.

chapters.summary: The psalmist is troubled at the prosperity of the wicked, but in the sanctuary he comes to understand their end, and so his trust in God is confirmed.
keyPoints: The psalmist admits his feet had almost slipped, for he envied the wicked when he saw their prosperity.
The wicked are proud and violent, yet their bodies are sleek and free of trouble, which confounds him.
The psalmist enters the sanctuary and considers the end of the wicked; he sees his own folly, and comes to hold God as his only portion.
chapters.application: When you resent the prosperity of the wicked, enter into God's presence, meditate on eternity, treasure God above all things, and find true security and satisfaction.

chapters.summary: The psalmist laments the destruction of the temple, asks God to remember his people, and is confident that God will bring judgment.
keyPoints: The psalmist asks God why he has cast off his people forever, and why his anger smokes against the sheep of his pasture.
He describes how enemies have destroyed the temple and defiled God's dwelling place.
The psalmist calls on God to remember the covenant he made and to punish the wicked.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, we may pour out our hearts to God as the psalmist did, trusting that he watches over his people and will bring about justice.

chapters.summary: Psalm 75 declares that God is the judge; he will judge righteously in his appointed time, bringing the proud low and lifting up the upright.
keyPoints: It gives thanks for God's wondrous deeds and proclaims his name.
God says: at the set time, I will judge with equity.
Let not the proud boast, for it is God alone who brings low and lifts up.
chapters.application: When the world is unjust, let us trust that God will judge righteously. Let us be humble, not boast, and commit everything into God's hands.

chapters.summary: Psalm 76 praises God's awesome presence in Jerusalem; he breaks the weapons of the enemy and judges the whole earth, bringing salvation to the humble.
keyPoints: God is known in Judah and great in Israel; his dwelling place is set in Salem.
God breaks the bow, the spear, and the shield of the enemy; the mighty men sleep, and their horses and chariots are stunned.
God alone is to be feared; he executes judgment to save all the humble of the earth.
chapters.application: When you are in hardship, remember that God is the judge of all the earth, and he protects the humble. Cast your burden on him and rest in reverence, for he will fight for you.

chapters.summary: In distress the psalmist cries to God, remembers God's past deeds, and turns from despair to hope, confident that God will bring deliverance.
keyPoints: The psalmist cries out in anguish in the night; his soul refuses to be comforted, troubled and restless.
He remembers God's deeds of old, meditates on God's might and holiness, and questions arise within his heart.
From this remembrance comes light; he becomes confident that God does wonders and redeems his people with his mighty power.
chapters.application: When you feel hopeless, recall the grace God has shown in your life, sing praise, and trust his faithfulness; he will lead you out of hardship.

chapters.summary: Psalm 78 reviews the history of Israel, reminding the people to remember God's deeds and not forget his law, lest they repeat their ancestors' rebellion.
keyPoints: It calls the people to give heed to instruction, telling the mysteries of old through parables and riddles.
It recounts God's wonders in the wilderness, such as water from the rock and manna from heaven, displaying his might.
It warns the people not to be like their ancestors, whose hearts were not steadfast and who murmured against God, but to respond with reverence.
chapters.application: Let us learn from history, continually number God's blessings, pass our faith on to the next generation, and respond to God's love with faith and obedience.

chapters.summary: Psalm 79 is a lament of Asaph, asking God to be angry at the nations who have defiled the temple, and asking God to forgive his people and punish their enemies, that his glory be displayed.
keyPoints: It laments that the temple has been destroyed, Jerusalem reduced to rubble, and the dead left as food for birds and beasts.
It asks God to show grace quickly, forgive the people's sins, and not be angry forever, for they have been brought very low.
It calls on God to avenge his people among the nations and repay their enemies; the people will answer his deliverance with praise, proclaiming his deeds to every generation.
chapters.application: When hardship comes or you see the church disgraced, pour out your heart to God, ask him to forgive and restore, and be confident that his mercy and justice will not delay.

chapters.summary: Psalm 80 is Asaph's prayer, asking God to restore Israel, as a shepherd leads his flock, to bring back his people.
keyPoints: It asks God to hear, as the shepherd who leads the house of Joseph, enthroned upon the cherubim.
It laments that God has made the people weep, becoming a byword to their neighbors, and asks God to turn back to them.
It asks God to care for this vine, to establish the branch he has planted, and to bring deliverance.
chapters.application: When we feel forsaken by God, let us cry out as the psalmist did for him to turn back to us, confident that he will restore us and make his face shine upon us.

chapters.summary: It calls the people to shout for joy and sing to God, remembering his deliverance and provision, and warns them not to harden their hearts but to listen to God's voice.
keyPoints: It calls the people to shout for joy and sing to God, remembering his deliverance and provision.
It recalls the exodus, reminding the people that God once delivered them from their burdens.
It warns the people that if they listen to God they will be satisfied and victorious, but otherwise they will be disciplined.
chapters.application: Let us continually remember the grace God has shown in our lives and answer him with joyful worship; let us also watch our hearts, refusing to be stiff-necked, submitting to God's leading, and enjoying the abundance he gives.

chapters.summary: Psalm 82 calls on God to judge among the gods, rebukes unjust rulers, and declares that God will govern all nations.
keyPoints: God stands in the midst of the mighty and judges unjust rulers.
He rebukes them for showing partiality to the wicked and failing to defend the weak and the needy.
Though called gods, they will die like men; the psalmist asks God to arise and judge the earth.
chapters.application: Examine whether you show favoritism when you hold power or status; follow God's example, uphold justice, and support the weak, for God will judge all peoples righteously.

chapters.summary: The psalmist asks God not to keep silent, and asks him to judge the enemies who conspire to destroy Israel, displaying his power.
keyPoints: The enemies take counsel together to cut off the name of Israel.
The psalmist lists the enemy nations and asks God to prevail over them as he has in the past.
He asks God to put them to shame, that they may know the LORD is the Most High.
chapters.application: When circumstances seem out of control and God seems silent, still trust in his sovereignty. Let us ask the Lord to make us humble, coming to know his holy name more deeply amid hardship.

chapters.summary: The psalmist longs for God's dwelling place, expressing how the pilgrim finds strength even in the Valley of Baca, for God is a sun and shield who gives grace and glory.
keyPoints: The psalmist deeply longs to dwell in God's house, delighting in the loveliness of his courts.
The pilgrim passing through the Valley of Baca finds it turned into a place of springs because God gives him strength.
A day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; blessed is the one who trusts in God.
chapters.application: However hard the circumstances, let us delight in God, for he is our strength and shield. On the road of seeking him, he will grant us grace and glory, giving us true satisfaction.

chapters.summary: Psalm 85 asks God to restore Israel, praises God's steadfast love and faithfulness, and looks forward to the meeting of righteousness and peace.
keyPoints: It recalls how God once forgave the people's iniquity and delivered them from captivity.
It asks God to grant restoration once more, to turn away his anger, and to let the people rejoice in him.
It declares that God's salvation is near to those who fear him, and his glory will fill the whole earth.
chapters.application: When we grow discouraged in hardship, let us remember God's past faithfulness, and ask him to restore us once more, trusting that his steadfast love and faithfulness will bring peace.

chapters.summary: In distress David cries to God, asks God to answer his prayer, and praises God's steadfast love and faithfulness, expressing his wholehearted devotion to God.
keyPoints: David asks God to incline his ear to his prayer, for he calls upon God all day long.
David acknowledges that God is good, ready to forgive, and abounding in steadfast love.
David asks God to teach him to walk in his truth, and to give him an undivided heart to fear his name.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us pour out our hearts to God as David did, trust deeply in his steadfast love and faithfulness, and ask him to guide us in the right path.

chapters.summary: Psalm 87 praises Zion as the city of God, foretells that all nations will belong to her, and shows that God himself has established her, making her glorious beyond compare.
keyPoints: God loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob, showing his special care for the holy city.
God enrolls the peoples in the book of life, including Egypt and Babylon, foreshadowing salvation for all the world.
Zion is called 'mother,' and all who come to faith are said to be born in her, for God himself has established her.
chapters.application: Wherever you come from, God receives you as his own people. Let us treasure our spiritual home with a thankful heart, and welcome all who turn to God.

chapters.summary: Psalm 88 is a lament crying out to God amid deep suffering; though the psalmist stands at the very brink of despair, he still persists in prayer.
keyPoints: The psalmist cries to God all day long, yet feels that God has hidden his face from him, his heart filled with darkness and pain.
He likens himself to one counted among the dead, forgotten by God, bearing God's wrath in the depths of the pit.
Even in his utter extremity, the psalmist does not give up praying to God, showing the resilience of faith.
chapters.application: When God seems far away, we may still pour out our hearts to him; prayer itself is an act of faith, and to keep crying out in the darkness is a courageous expression of belief.

chapters.summary: The psalmist extols the covenant God made with David; though he sees the dynasty in trouble, he still holds fast to God's faithfulness and steadfast love.
keyPoints: He sings of God's steadfast love and faithfulness, and of the covenant established with David.
He describes God's mighty rule over heaven and earth, righteousness and steadfast love going together.
He laments the king's disgrace, yet still asks God to remember the covenant he made.
chapters.application: When life seems to contradict God's promises, still trust in God's faithfulness, hold fast to hope in prayer, for God's covenant never changes.

chapters.summary: Psalm 90 is a prayer of Moses, lamenting the brevity of human life and asking God to grant wisdom and show mercy, that his people may enjoy his favor.
keyPoints: God is our eternal dwelling place, from everlasting to everlasting.
Human life is brief as grass, full of toil and sighing, passing quickly away.
He asks God to teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom and turn back to him.
chapters.application: In our limited days, let us ask God for wisdom, treasure each day, live with reverence, and look to God's steadfast love, that our lives be filled with meaning.

chapters.summary: Psalm 91 declares that God is the refuge of the faithful, protecting those who trust in him amid danger.
keyPoints: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest under the shadow of the Almighty.
God will deliver you from the snare of the fowler and from the deadly pestilence.
Because you love God with your whole heart, he will deliver you and grant you honor and long life.
chapters.application: Whatever fear or hardship you face, meditate on God's promises and trust him wholeheartedly; he will be with you as your high tower and refuge.

chapters.summary: This is a thanksgiving psalm praising God's steadfast love and faithfulness, declaring that the righteous will flourish while the wicked will perish.
keyPoints: It gives thanks to the LORD and sings praise to the Most High, proclaiming his steadfast love and faithfulness.
The LORD is an upright rock, in whom there is no unrighteousness, and he is worthy of all praise and honor.
Though the wicked flourish like grass they will perish forever; the righteous, like the palm tree, will still bear fruit in old age, testifying to God's faithfulness.
chapters.application: In good times remember to give thanks to God; in hard times hold fast to his justice. Root yourself in God like a palm tree, bearing fruit even in old age, testifying to his faithfulness.

chapters.summary: Psalm 93 extols the LORD as king, ruling the world in majesty and might; his throne can never be shaken.
keyPoints: The LORD is robed in majesty and girded with strength; the world is established and cannot be moved.
The floods lift up their waves, but the LORD on high is mightier than the waters.
The LORD's testimonies are sure; holiness adorns his house forever.
chapters.application: Facing an unsettled world, remember that God reigns and his promises stand firm; rest in him with reverence and faith.

chapters.summary: The psalmist cries out for God to bring justice, rebukes the proud and oppressive wicked, and is confident that God will discipline and comfort those who belong to him.
keyPoints: He asks God to rise up and judge the proud and wicked, and to make his justice known.
The wicked think God does not see as they oppress the people, but God does see.
God disciplines those who belong to him, grants peace, and gives the righteous victory.
chapters.application: When you face injustice, pour out your heart to God, confident that he watches over you, gain wisdom through discipline, and find comfort in hardship.

chapters.summary: It calls the people to worship God with joy and thanksgiving, while warning them not to harden their hearts as their ancestors did in the wilderness, but to listen to God's voice.
keyPoints: Come, let us sing to the LORD; let us make a joyful shout to the rock of our salvation.
Let us come before him with thanksgiving and praise, for he is a great King who reigns over all.
Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah and Massah; listen to God's voice and enter into his rest.
chapters.application: Worship God each day with a thankful heart, listen for his voice, and do not repeat Israel's rebellion, but enter by faith into the rest he gives.

chapters.summary: It calls all nations to sing a new song to the LORD, proclaiming his salvation and glory, for he will judge the world in righteousness.
keyPoints: It invites the whole earth to sing praise to the LORD, proclaiming his salvation and wondrous deeds.
It declares that the LORD is a great God, far above all gods, to be worshiped in the beauty of holiness.
It calls all peoples to tremble before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth, ruling in righteousness and faithfulness.
chapters.application: Answer God's greatness each day with fresh praise, proclaim his salvation in every part of your life, and keep his righteousness and faithfulness in mind as you face his judgment without fear.

chapters.summary: Psalm 97 declares that the LORD reigns, emphasizing his majesty and righteousness, and calls all peoples to worship, while the righteous rejoice in him.
keyPoints: The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice, let the many coastlands be glad.
God displays his majesty with fire, lightning, and earthquake, causing his enemies to tremble.
The LORD loves righteousness, protects the righteous, hates idols, and will judge the whole earth.
chapters.application: Facing injustice in the world, remember that God reigns and will bring justice. Let us hate evil, love God, worship him with joy, for he protects those who faithfully follow him.

chapters.summary: Psalm 98 calls the whole earth to sing a new song to the LORD, for he accomplishes wondrous salvation through righteousness and steadfast love.
keyPoints: The LORD reveals his righteousness in the sight of the nations, doing salvation and remembering his steadfast love and faithfulness.
The whole earth is to shout for joy to the LORD, praising him loudly with harp, song, and trumpet.
The LORD comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity.
chapters.application: Remember God's saving deeds throughout history, praise him with joy and song, and be confident that he will judge the earth in righteousness, so let us live with reverence and hope.

chapters.summary: Psalm 99 praises the LORD as king, emphasizing his holiness and righteousness, and calls the people to worship him.
keyPoints: The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth quake.
The LORD is great in Zion, exalted above all peoples; let them praise his great and awesome name.
The LORD executes justice and righteousness; he hears prayer and forgives his people, yet repays them according to their deeds.
chapters.application: Let us honor God's holiness, worship him with reverence, and be confident that he hears our prayers, living with righteousness and mercy.

chapters.summary: Psalm 100 calls all the earth to make a joyful noise to the LORD, to enter his gates with thanksgiving and praise, and to give thanks for his everlasting steadfast love and faithfulness.
keyPoints: Let all the earth shout for joy to God, serve him with gladness, and come before him singing.
Know that the LORD is God; he made us, and we are his people, the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, praise him in his courts, for he is good, and his steadfast love endures forever.
chapters.application: Come before God each day with a thankful heart, remembering that he is the source of all that is good, and that his steadfast love and faithfulness never change -- this gives us hope and peace even in hardship.

chapters.summary: David declares that he will govern with mercy and justice; he resolves to turn away from wickedness, remain faithful to God, and surround himself with the faithful.
keyPoints: The psalmist resolves to sing of mercy and justice, and to walk before God with a blameless heart.
He determines to set no wicked thing before his eyes, to hate the work of those who turn aside, and to allow no evil to cling to him.
He chooses to dwell only with the faithful, cutting off the wicked from the land day by day, to keep the holy city pure.
chapters.application: Let us resolve to walk with integrity at home and at work, turn away from evil, choose to walk with the godly, and let God's principles guide our daily lives.

chapters.summary: In deep affliction the psalmist cries out to God, confident that he will show favor to Zion and restore her glory, revealing God's eternity and faithfulness.
keyPoints: In his distress, body and soul wasting away like smoke, the psalmist begs God to answer him speedily.
He suffers from his enemies' taunts and from God's wrath, groaning day and night, unable to eat his bread.
Yet he is confident that God will have mercy on Zion and rebuild the holy city, so that all nations will fear him, for God is eternal and unchanging.
chapters.application: When we feel lonely and helpless, we can pour out our hearts to God as the psalmist did, trusting that he hears our prayers and will bring comfort and restoration in his own time.

chapters.summary: David blesses the LORD, counting up his benefits, and calls on all creation to praise him for his mercy and steadfast love.
keyPoints: Bless the LORD, and forget not all his benefits.
He forgives all our iniquities, heals all our diseases, redeems our life from destruction, and crowns us with lovingkindness and tender mercies.
He is merciful; he does not always chide, nor keep his anger forever, but pities us as a father pities his children.
chapters.application: Today, let us count God's blessings, bless him with a grateful heart, and, moved by his mercy and steadfast love, learn to forgive and show kindness to others.

chapters.summary: The psalmist praises the LORD's greatness and wisdom in creating all things, and declares that his glory endures forever.
keyPoints: The psalmist opens with praise, extolling God's honor and majesty, who covers himself with light as with a garment.
He describes how God created the heavens and the earth, the seas and the mountains, and every living creature, revealing his mighty power.
God cares for all his creatures, giving them food in due season so that all things grow and both man and beast are satisfied.
chapters.application: May we always look upon nature with awe, seeing in it God's wondrous works, giving thanks for his care, and praising him day by day.

chapters.summary: Psalm 105 calls God's chosen people to remember the covenant he made with Abraham, and recounts his wondrous works in guiding and delivering Israel throughout history.
keyPoints: Give thanks to the LORD, call upon his name, and make known his deeds among the peoples.
Remember the wonders he has done, his marvelous works, and the judgments he has spoken.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded, which he established with Abraham.
chapters.application: Today, let us continually count God's blessings, remember his works in our lives, respond to his faithfulness with faith, and make his name known before others.

chapters.summary: This psalm reviews Israel's rebellion in the wilderness and God's mercy, calling his chosen people to praise him and pray for revival.
keyPoints: Praise God for his steadfast love and wondrous works, calling his chosen people to give him thanks.
The psalm recounts Israel's repeated rebellions in the wilderness, revealing the weakness of human nature.
For his own name's sake, God forgave them again and again, showing his mercy and faithfulness.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's past grace, confess our own failings, cry out for revival with a grateful heart, and live out trust and obedience today.

chapters.summary: Psalm 107 calls God's people to give thanks to the LORD, for he has redeemed them from trouble, displaying his steadfast love and wondrous works.
keyPoints: It calls the redeemed to give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, and his mercy endures forever.
It recounts his deliverance from various distresses — wandering in the wilderness, imprisonment in darkness, sickness and affliction, and peril at sea.
It exhorts us to consider the LORD's steadfast love, to observe his works with wisdom, and to offer him thanksgiving.
chapters.application: When you cry out to the Lord in trouble, he will hear and deliver you. Keep a grateful heart, count his blessings, and do not forget to praise his steadfast love even in times of ease.

chapters.summary: Psalm 108 is a psalm of praise and petition by David, declaring God's mighty power and faithfulness, and asking him to help Israel triumph over her enemies.
keyPoints: With a steadfast heart, the psalmist sings praises to God's steadfast love and faithfulness at the break of dawn.
He cries out for God to answer his prayer, to save his beloved people, and to defeat their enemies.
He is confident of victory through God, for God has promised triumph over Edom and Philistia.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us praise God first, trusting that his faithfulness will lead us to overcome every difficulty.

chapters.summary: When attacked by wicked men, David cries out for God to vindicate him, foretells the wicked's judgment, and ends the psalm with praise and trust in God.
keyPoints: David pours out to God the malice and unprovoked attacks of his enemies, pleading with him not to keep silent.
In the form of an imprecatory psalm, David cries out for justice, asking God to punish the wicked and their descendants.
Even in his suffering, David still cries out to God for help, confident that God will deliver him.
chapters.application: When we suffer injustice, we can pour out our hearts to God as David did, trusting that he will vindicate us, and continue to face our trials with praise and trust.

chapters.summary: Psalm 110 prophesies the Messiah's identity as both king and priest, emphasizing God's authority and judgment.
keyPoints: The LORD says to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.'
'You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek' — revealing the office of Christ.
The Lord will judge the nations in his wrath, striking down kings and executing judgment in his anger.
chapters.application: Let us trust in Christ as our King and Priest, look to his power in times of trouble, revere God's righteous judgment, and live lives of holiness and obedience.

chapters.summary: Psalm 111 praises God's works, extols his steadfast love and faithfulness, and teaches that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
keyPoints: The psalmist gives thanks to the LORD with his whole heart, praising his works in the assembly of the upright.
God's works are great, righteous, and faithful; his precepts are trustworthy and stand fast forever.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and all who obey his commandments are blessed.
chapters.application: Today, let us meditate on God's wondrous works, obey his word with reverence, rely on his faithfulness in all things, and gain true wisdom and blessing.

chapters.summary: This psalm praises those who fear the LORD and delight in his commandments, describing their blessed state in contrast to the fate of the wicked.
keyPoints: Those who fear God and delight greatly in his commandments will be blessed, and their descendants will be mighty.
Light rises in the darkness for the upright, who are gracious, generous, and righteous.
The wicked see it and are angered; they gnash their teeth and melt away, and their desire shall perish.
chapters.application: Let us today take delight in the fear of God, love his word, show righteousness by being gracious to others, and trust that God will establish us so that we will not be moved.

chapters.summary: Psalm 113 calls the servants of the LORD to praise him, emphasizing that though he is exalted above all, he cares for the lowly and gives children to the barren, revealing his grace.
keyPoints: It calls the servants of the LORD to praise him from this time forth and forevermore.
The LORD is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.
He raises up the poor and makes the barren woman the joyful mother of children.
chapters.application: Whatever your station in life, remember that God cares for the lowly. Praise him in your affliction, for he will lift you up and grant you unexpected blessings.

chapters.summary: Psalm 114 recalls the miracles of Israel's exodus from Egypt, praising God's mighty power over nature and in redeeming his people.
keyPoints: When Israel went out of Egypt, God parted the Red Sea and turned the Jordan River back.
The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like young lambs, showing how creation itself trembles before its Creator.
Let the whole earth tremble before the LORD, who turns the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring.
chapters.application: Recall God's wondrous works in your life — even when circumstances seem impossible, he can still make a way. Today, trust him with a heart of reverence and gratitude.

chapters.summary: The psalmist calls for glory to be given to God for his steadfast love and faithfulness, denounces the emptiness of idols, urges the house of Israel to trust in the LORD, and declares that God will bless those who fear him.
keyPoints: Not to us, O LORD, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
Idols have mouths but cannot speak, eyes but cannot see; those who make them become like them.
Let the house of Israel trust in the LORD; he is their help and their shield.
chapters.application: Give glory to God, and do not trust in idols made by human hands. In times of trouble, trust wholly in the Lord who made heaven and earth, and he will bless you and your household.

chapters.summary: The psalmist gives thanks for being delivered from death, resolves to call upon the LORD as long as he lives, and pays his vows before all the people, praising God.
keyPoints: The psalmist declares that God has heard his supplication, and so he will call upon him as long as he lives.
He describes how the cords of death and the pains of Sheol had entangled him, but he called upon the LORD and was delivered.
With a grateful heart, he offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving and pays his vows before all the people, in the courts of Jerusalem.
chapters.application: When we cry out to God in trouble, he will hear us. Let us keep a grateful heart, testify to God's grace before others, and fulfill the vows we have made to him.

chapters.summary: Psalm 117 calls all nations and peoples to praise the LORD, for his steadfast love and faithfulness endure forever.
keyPoints: It calls all nations and peoples to praise God, for his steadfast love and faithfulness are great.
Though the shortest of psalms, it carries a call to worldwide mission, pointing to worship across the whole earth.
It emphasizes that God's steadfast love and faithfulness are the foundation for praise, and they never change.
chapters.application: Wherever we find ourselves, let us remember God's steadfast love and faithfulness, respond to his grace with praise, and make his name known.

chapters.summary: Psalm 118 is a psalm of thanksgiving and victory, praising God's steadfast love and faithfulness, and encouraging his people to trust in the LORD in times of trouble.
keyPoints: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his steadfast love endures forever.
In distress I called upon the LORD; he answered me and set me in a large place.
The stone the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone — this is the day that the LORD has made.
chapters.application: Whether in ease or hardship, let us give thanks to God, for his steadfast love never changes. Call upon him in trouble, and he will grant peace and deliverance, making us more than conquerors.

chapters.summary: Psalm 119, the longest chapter in the Bible, is an acrostic poem of twenty-two stanzas that repeatedly extols the preciousness of God's word, teaching that those who keep his law are blessed.
keyPoints: Blessed are those who are blameless in their ways and walk in the law of the LORD, for they receive his favor.
The psalmist resolves to seek God with a pure heart, asking him to teach him his statutes.
In times of trouble, God's word becomes comfort and hope, so that one need not be ashamed.
chapters.application: Take time each day to read Scripture and let God's word guide your steps; meditate on it in times of hardship, and you will find strength and direction.

chapters.summary: Psalm 120, the first of the Songs of Ascents, is the psalmist's plea for deliverance from lying and deceitful men, and an expression of his longing for peace.
keyPoints: In his distress the psalmist cried to the LORD, and he answered him.
The psalmist denounces the lying lips and deceitful tongue, asking God to bring judgment.
He laments dwelling among Meshech and the tents of Kedar, longing for peace while surrounded by war.
chapters.application: When we find ourselves surrounded by injustice or strife, let us cry out to God as the psalmist did, hold fast to the pursuit of peace, and trust that God will hear us.

chapters.summary: Psalm 121 is a song of trust in God's protection, declaring that the LORD watches over us at all times and keeps us in our going out and our coming in.
keyPoints: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the hills, confident that his help comes from the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
God neither slumbers nor sleeps; he watches over and protects his people day and night.
