The LORD will keep us from all harm, from this time forth and forevermore.
chapters.application: Wherever you find yourself, lift your eyes to God, and he will watch over you. He guards you day and night and will not let your foot slip. May this peace accompany your going out and your coming in, from this time forth and forevermore.

chapters.summary: The psalmist expresses his love for Jerusalem, calls for prayer for the peace of the holy city, and praises the thrones of judgment set within it.
keyPoints: The psalmist rejoices to go up to Jerusalem to worship, for there stands the house of the LORD.
Jerusalem is the city to which the tribes go up, a testimony to Israel.
It calls for prayer for the peace of Jerusalem, that she may prosper and her palaces be secure.
chapters.application: Today let us pray for peace in our church and community, join in worship with a joyful heart, and long for God's righteousness and peace to be made known among us.

chapters.summary: The psalmist looks to God and pleads for mercy, for they have had more than enough of contempt from the world and scorn from the proud.
keyPoints: The psalmist lifts his eyes to God, as the eyes of a servant look to the hand of his master, expressing complete dependence.
He asks for mercy, for they have been treated with contempt beyond measure, and their hearts are filled with anguish.
In the face of scorn from the proud, the psalmist still holds fast to his faith, waiting for God to answer.
chapters.application: When you are despised or scorned, lift your eyes to God as the psalmist did, and ask for his mercy — he will hear your cry and give you strength to face it.

chapters.summary: This psalm praises the LORD for delivering Israel from the hand of her enemies, like a bird escaping the snare of the fowler.
keyPoints: If the LORD had not been on our side, our enemies would long ago have swallowed us up.
Though the raging waters surged over us, the LORD kept us from being swept away.
We have escaped like a bird from the fowler's snare, by the help of the name of the LORD.
chapters.application: Remember God's past deliverance, trust that he still watches over you in your troubles, and rely on him with a grateful heart.

chapters.summary: Psalm 125 teaches that those who trust in the LORD are as firm as Mount Zion; God will protect his people and grant peace to the upright.
keyPoints: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, for God surrounds and protects them.
The scepter of wickedness will not remain over the land allotted to the righteous, lest the righteous themselves turn their hands to evil.
It prays that God will do good to the upright, and lead away the workers of iniquity along with the wicked; God grants peace to Israel and guides them in the right way.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us trust firmly in God — he will surround us like the mountains and grant us peace. May the Lord keep us walking in uprightness and far from evil.

chapters.summary: Psalm 126 tells of the joy and petition of those returning from exile, expressing gratitude and hope for God's restoration of his people's fortunes.
keyPoints: It recalls the joy of returning from captivity — like a dream, with mouths filled with laughter and singing.
The nations saw God's great power and acknowledged that the LORD had done great things for Israel.
It prays that God will restore the captives like streams flowing again in the Negev, confident that those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us remember God's past deliverance and face today's challenges with faith, for those who sow in tears will surely reap with joy.

chapters.summary: Psalm 127 stresses that all building and guarding belong to the LORD — only by trusting in God can a household and a life be built and kept in peace.
keyPoints: Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain.
The LORD gives sleep to those he loves, showing that both labor and rest are in God's hands, and we should trust in his provision.
Children are a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward from him, like arrows in the hand of a warrior.
chapters.application: Whether in work or family today, let us seek God's will first, entrust our burdens to him, and trust in his care, so that we may enjoy true rest.

chapters.summary: Those who fear the LORD and walk in his ways will be blessed, and both their household and their city will enjoy peace and prosperity.
keyPoints: Those who fear God and walk in his ways are blessed; they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
His wife will be like a fruitful vine, and his children like olive shoots, a sign of a flourishing household.
May the LORD bless him from Zion, that he may see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of his life, and peace upon his children's children.
chapters.application: May you fear God each day and walk in his word, experiencing his blessing in your family and work, and enjoying peace and contentment.

chapters.summary: Israel looks back on her past afflictions, confident that the LORD is righteous and will put her enemies to shame, and prays that God will bless those who love him.
keyPoints: The psalmist recalls Israel's afflictions from her youth, yet stresses that God never let her enemies prevail over her.
He prays that the wicked will wither like grass on the rooftops, unable to bear fruit — a sign that their fate is judgment from God.
He declares that the LORD is righteous; he will cut apart the cords of the wicked and protect his people.
chapters.application: However much affliction we face, let us trust firmly that God watches over us — his righteousness will surely be revealed. Let us hold fast to faith and wait for his salvation.

chapters.summary: Psalm 130 is a penitential psalm; the psalmist cries out to God from the depths, looking for his forgiveness and redemption, and urges Israel to wait for the LORD, for he has steadfast love and abundant redemption.
keyPoints: Out of the depths the psalmist cries to God, asking the Lord to hear his voice and to forgive his sins.
He waits for the Lord's word, as watchmen wait for the morning, longing earnestly for God's salvation.
He urges Israel to hope in the LORD, for with him is steadfast love and abundant redemption, and he will redeem his people from all their iniquities.
chapters.application: When you feel crushed by sin, do not despair — cry out to God from the depths as the psalmist did. Be confident that he offers forgiving grace, wait patiently for him, and he will redeem you from all your iniquities.

chapters.summary: The psalmist trusts in God with a humble and quiet heart, like a weaned child in its mother's arms, and calls on Israel to hope in the LORD from this time forth and forevermore.
keyPoints: The psalmist confesses that his heart is not proud, his eyes are not haughty, and he does not concern himself with great matters too wonderful for him.
He has calmed and quieted his soul, like a weaned child with its mother, no longer troubled by the affairs of the world.
He calls Israel to hope in the LORD, from this time forth and forevermore, for God is trustworthy.
chapters.application: In the busyness of life, learn to be still before God, laying down pride and anxiety, and trust him as a child does, so that you may enjoy peace within.

chapters.summary: Psalm 132 commemorates David's vow to the LORD, prays that God will remember David's hardships, and blesses Zion and God's anointed one, emphasizing God's promise to the house of David.
keyPoints: David swore an oath to find a dwelling place for the LORD, allowing himself neither sleep nor rest until he did.
God chose Zion as his everlasting resting place and blessed it richly.
God promised that David's descendants would sit on his throne forever, on condition that they keep his covenant.
chapters.application: Let us follow David's zeal, responding to God with action, trusting firmly that his promises will be fulfilled, and holding on to faith while we wait.

chapters.summary: Psalm 133 praises the goodness of brothers dwelling together in unity, like precious oil and refreshing dew, bringing God's blessing and life forevermore.
keyPoints: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity — like precious oil poured on the head.
Such unity is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion, bringing refreshment.
For there the LORD has commanded the blessing — life forevermore.
chapters.application: At home or in church, actively pursue unity, treating one another with humility and love, so that God's blessing may fall like dew, filling you with joy and peace.

chapters.summary: Psalm 134 calls all the servants of the LORD to bless him in the temple at night, and prays that God will bless the worshippers from Zion.
keyPoints: It invites all the servants of the LORD who stand by night in his house to bless him.
It emphasizes lifting up hands toward the sanctuary in prayer and praising God's name.
It prays that the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth, will bless them out of Zion.
chapters.application: Whether day or night, we can bless God at any time. In busy moments or quiet ones, lift up your hands in prayer, trusting that the God who made heaven and earth will bless us from Zion.

chapters.summary: Psalm 135 calls the people to praise the LORD for his greatness, his power, and his choosing of Israel, and denounces the emptiness of idols.
keyPoints: It calls God's chosen people to praise him, for he is good and his name is pleasant.
It declares God's sovereignty over nature and history, far above all other gods.
It mocks the powerlessness of idols, urging the house of Israel to trust in the LORD alone.
chapters.application: Remind yourself each day that God is Lord over all things and his works are wonderful. Give glory to him, and do not trust in the empty idols made by human hands.

chapters.summary: Psalm 136 is a psalm of thanksgiving, repeatedly declaring that God's steadfast love endures forever, giving thanks for his mighty works in creating the heavens and earth, delivering Israel, and caring for all peoples.
keyPoints: All twenty-six verses of the psalm end with the refrain 'for his steadfast love endures forever,' emphasizing God's unchanging grace.
From the creation of the heavens and the earth to the redemption of Israel, it reviews God's mighty works throughout history.
It calls the assembly to give thanks together to the God of gods and the Lord of lords, for his steadfast love endures forever.
chapters.application: Whether in ease or hardship, let us count God's blessings in our lives and keep a grateful heart, for his steadfast love endures forever and is our daily strength and support.

chapters.summary: Psalm 137 expresses the deep longing of the Jews exiled in Babylon for Zion, along with intense pleas for God to bring retribution on their enemies.
keyPoints: By the rivers of Babylon, the Jews wept as they remembered Zion, unable to sing the songs of the LORD.
They refused to make music in a foreign land, resolving to let their right hand wither and their tongue cling to the roof of their mouth rather than forget Jerusalem.
The psalmist prays for God to remember the evil the Edomites did, and declares that Babylon will be repaid, expressing his devotion to the holy city through this lament of imprecation.
chapters.application: When we are in a foreign land or in hardship, let us still hold fast to our faith, remember God's works, entrust our pain to him, and trust that he will bring justice.

chapters.summary: In hardship, David gives thanks to God for his steadfast love and faithfulness, confident that God will fulfill his purpose for him.
keyPoints: David gives thanks to God with his whole heart, singing his praise before the gods, showing his undivided worship of God.
God heard David's cry and gave him strength, making him bold and strong in the day of trouble.
Though God is exalted above the heavens, he regards the lowly and fulfills the desires of those who fear him.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us give thanks to God with grateful hearts, confident that his steadfast love endures forever, that he cares for the lowly, and that he will fulfill our heart's desires.

chapters.summary: The psalmist praises God's omniscience, omnipresence, and omnipotence, and asks him to search his heart and lead him, expressing a deep knowledge of and dependence on God.
keyPoints: God knows everything about me, even my very thoughts.
I cannot flee from God's presence, for he is everywhere.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made; I ask God to search me and lead me.
chapters.application: Wherever you are, God watches over you. In times of confusion, ask him to search your heart and lead you in the way everlasting, and he will keep you.

chapters.summary: David asks God to deliver him from the schemes and attacks of the wicked, confident that God will vindicate the afflicted, and calls for judgment on the wicked.
keyPoints: David pleads with God to deliver him from violent and scheming men.
The wicked have set snares and traps for him, and David asks God for protection.
David is confident that God will vindicate the afflicted, and the wicked will be repaid.
chapters.application: When you face injustice or secret schemes against you, pour out your heart to God as David did, trusting that he watches over you, will vindicate you, and will keep your heart at peace.

chapters.summary: In danger, David asks God to hear his prayer, pleads with him to guard his words and thoughts, is willing to accept the rebuke of the righteous, and asks God to judge the wicked.
keyPoints: He asks that his prayer be heard, and accepted like the evening sacrifice.
He asks God to guard his mouth, that his heart may not turn to evil deeds or the schemes of wicked men.
He welcomes the rebuke of the righteous as a kindness like oil, while judgment must come upon the wicked.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us first ask God to guard our hearts and mouths, to keep us far from evil, humbly accept correction from those who walk with God, leave judgment to him, and look wholly to his deliverance.

chapters.summary: Psalm 142 is the psalmist's prayer, pouring out his heart to God in trouble, expressing his trust in and cry to God when he feels alone and helpless.
keyPoints: The psalmist cries aloud to God, pouring out his complaint, asking to be heard.
When enemies have secretly laid snares for him and no one takes notice to help him, the Lord alone is his refuge.
The psalmist asks God for deliverance, believing that God will show him favor and bring him out of prison.
chapters.application: When you feel alone and helpless, pour out your heart to God as the psalmist did, trusting firmly that he is our refuge — he will watch over us and lead us out of our troubles.

chapters.summary: In his affliction the psalmist cries out to God, confesses his own weakness, pleads for God to lead him according to his faithfulness and righteousness, and asks God's Spirit to guide him along level ground.
keyPoints: The psalmist asks God to hear his prayer, for the enemy has pursued him and his spirit grows faint within him.
He remembers God's deeds of old and stretches out his hands to him, his soul like a parched land.
He pleads with God to answer him quickly and to send his good Spirit to lead him out of trouble.
chapters.application: When you feel you have nowhere to turn, remember that God is faithful — he will hear our cry and guide us in the right way.

chapters.summary: David prays for God to grant victory and peace, praises God as the rock of his strength, and looks forward to the prosperity and security of his people.
keyPoints: He praises God as the one who trains his hands for war and gives him strength.
He prays for God to intervene in battle and save him from the attacks of foreigners.
He paints a picture of a blessed people's prosperity and peace.
chapters.application: In the face of life's challenges, rely on God's power, ask him to grant peace and abundance, and treasure the blessings he gives.

chapters.summary: David extols God's greatness, grace, and steadfast love, encouraging every generation to declare his works and his kingdom.
keyPoints: David resolves to bless God every day and to praise his name forever and ever.
God is great and his greatness is unsearchable; people must declare his mighty works.
God is gracious, merciful, and loving; he is good to all and cares for everyone who calls upon him.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us look for opportunities each day to praise God, count his blessings, and tell the next generation of his works, so that more may come to know his steadfast love.

chapters.summary: The psalmist calls for praise to the LORD, emphasizing that he is a faithful, righteous, and loving God who cares for the afflicted, and warns against relying on mortal man.
keyPoints: The psalmist calls his whole being to praise the LORD, for he is worthy of praise.
Do not put your trust in mortal man, for when his breath departs, he returns to the dust.
The LORD made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them; he keeps faith forever.
chapters.application: Today, let us turn our eyes from man and circumstances to God, our faithful helper. Whatever we face, let us offer him the sacrifice of praise, for he will watch over us.

chapters.summary: This psalm praises God's mighty power, care, and redemption, encouraging us to respond to his grace with song and thanksgiving.
keyPoints: God builds up Jerusalem and gathers the outcasts of Israel, showing his care.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds, comforting the lowly.
He sustains all things by his power, giving food to the beasts and to the young ravens, revealing his provision.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us praise God in song, for he cares for the lowly and gives strength to those who seek him.

chapters.summary: The psalmist calls on all creation, in heaven and on earth, to praise the LORD together, for his glory is above the earth and the heavens, and he has raised up his people.
keyPoints: The psalmist calls the sun, moon, and stars, the angels and heavenly hosts, to praise God.
All things on earth — sea creatures, fire, mountains, trees, wild animals, and creeping things — are to praise him.
All peoples — kings, rulers, young men and maidens alike — are to praise the LORD, for his name alone is exalted.
chapters.application: Today, we too can invite everything around us to join in praising God, seeing his greatness in ordinary life, and responding to his care with grateful hearts.

chapters.summary: Psalm 149 calls God's chosen people to praise him, for God delights in his people and grants them victory and honor.
keyPoints: It encourages the people to sing a new song of praise to God in the assembly of the godly, for he is their Maker and King.
God takes pleasure in his humble people; he adorns them with salvation and honors the afflicted.
The saints are to have the high praises of God in their mouths and a two-edged sword in their hand, to carry out his judgment.
chapters.application: Today, let us praise God with joyful hearts, not only with our words but with lives of obedience. God is our glory and strength — he will fight for us and make us more than conquerors.

chapters.summary: Psalm 150 calls all who have breath to praise the LORD with every kind of instrument, forming a glorious conclusion to the book of Psalms.
keyPoints: Praise God in his sanctuary and in his mighty heavens, for his mighty deeds and his surpassing greatness.
Praise him loudly with trumpet, lute and harp, timbrel and dance, strings and pipe, and clashing cymbals.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD — the whole book closes with Hallelujah.
chapters.application: Today, whatever our circumstances, let us offer God praise in spirit and truth, for he is worthy of all honor.
